summary: # CLO Skills Mini Classroom - Automatic Dressing Tool ## Introduction Today, we will learn how to use the Automatic Clothing Tool. This tool can significantly streamline the process of dressing virtual models in CLO. ## Using the Default Model For example, when the model is the default model of CLO and the costume is completed, you may need to adjust the model size or change the horse. Here’s how to automatically wear a 3D costume for the virtual model: 1. This is a file with code information. 2. Click on the 3D model in the window of the object to match the 3D model. 3. Select the model of the corresponding size in the folder. 4. Click on the Automatic Clothing Tool in the 3D toolbar. You can see that the costume is completed very quickly according to the model size. The remaining two horses can also undergo the same operation: 1. Change the size of the object window and match the 3D shape. 2. Click on the Automatic Clothing Tool in the 3D toolbar. In this way, you can quickly complete the costume cladding corresponding to the size. ## Final Size Adjustment Next is the last size, which follows the same procedure as the previous operations. You can quickly complete the production of this horse-riding file: 1. In the menu bar, find "Production" and select "Check Horse." 2. Now you can see the cladding effect of each size on one page. ## Working with External Models Example 2: When you need to use an external model, be aware that the external model cannot use the Automatic Clothing Tool directly. You need to match the 3D model with the costume first. 1. In the menu bar, find "Virtual Model" and select the "Virtual Model Editor." 2. In the top section of the Virtual Model Editor, locate the "Costume Cladding." ### Creating a Costume There are two ways to create a costume: - **Automatic Clothing Tool**: 1. In the upper right corner, click the Automatic Clothing Tool button. 2. You will see a gray version shadow around the model. 3. Click the Automatic Clothing Tool button at the bottom. 4. Rotate to check if the red costume cladding around the model is flat. In this way, the costume cladding of the model is completed. If the costume cladding is not created correctly, you will need to use manual creation. ### Manual Creation of Costume Cladding To manually create the costume cladding, follow these steps: 1. Draw a line on the model according to the instructions on the mouse. 2. First, draw a neckline by placing three dots on the neck. 3. Next, follow the same method to complete the rest of the parts. 4. Click the "Automatically Create a Costume Cladding" button at the bottom of the list. 5. Click on the button below the list to finalize the costume cladding. Once the creation is completed, click "Save" to save the model with the costume cladding. ## Replacing the Model Now let’s see how to replace the model: 1. Open the model directly. 2. Use the switch to change the model. 3. In the 3D toolbar, click on "Automatic Clothing." You will see that the model has been replaced successfully. Repeat the clicking of "Automatic Clothing" in the 3D toolbar to ensure the new model is dressed correctly.
